scams.name: Fake Site Closure Redirect
scams.setup: A local shouts that a gate/street/site is closed for prayer or a holiday.
scams.mechanism: Redirects toward a shop or paid animal ride under manufactured urgency.
scams.countermeasure: Verify at the actual official ticket booth/turnstile, never take a street tout's word for site status.

scams.name: Unlicensed 'Guide' Approach
scams.setup: Men outside sites present themselves as guides without credentials.
scams.mechanism: Provides fabricated historical claims for a tip; no accountability since not actually licensed.
scams.countermeasure: Book licensed guides in advance through your hotel or a vetted tour operator; verify credentials on the spot if approached.

scams.name: The Tomb 'Secret Area' / Fan Trap
scams.setup: A guard hands over an item (cardboard fan, points at 'secret' carving) unsolicited inside a tomb.
scams.mechanism: Creates a false sense of a rendered 'service' that obligates a tip; guard may act disappointed regardless of amount given to escalate further.
scams.countermeasure: Decline any unsolicited item or 'special access' immediately; don't accept objects from strangers inside sites.

scams.name: Camel/Horse Ride Extortion
scams.setup: Handler quotes a low price to mount the animal.
scams.mechanism: Once out in the desert away from other people, demands a much larger sum to make the animal kneel/return, functionally holding the rider hostage.
scams.countermeasure: Confirm total price, currency, and duration in writing/photo before mounting; avoid deals made far from the main entrance.

scams.name: Commission-Driven Guiding
scams.setup: Even legitimate hired guides may rush historical explanations to spend more time at partner shops.
scams.mechanism: Guide receives a commission on anything purchased at the stop.
scams.countermeasure: Set expectations upfront ('I'm not shopping today') and choose guides via reviews that don't mention shop stops.
